course_name_original: Electrical power equipment and switching stations
course_name_en: Electrical power equipment and switching stations

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows the construction of electrical devices used in the generation, transmission, distribution and utilization of electrical energy.
The student knows the threats to electrical power equipment and switching stations.
The student can calculate characteristic electrical quantities determining the selection of electrical power devices and apparatus under normal operation and during fault conditions.
The student can independently conduct laboratory tests of various electrical devices and apparatus to assess their condition and functional efficiency.
The student is able to work in a group during measurements and project execution.

syllabus_topics: Design of an industrial power supply system for electrical energy consumers: 1. Determination of peak powers for individual objects and the entire plant using the power demand factor method. 2. Selection of capacitor banks to improve the power factor. 3. Selection of transformers. 4. Determination of characteristic short-circuit values on the MV and LV sides. 5. Location of the electrical power station. 6. Selection of MV and LV switchgear bays based on prefabricated elements available in the country. 7. Arrangement of equipment (switchgear, capacitor banks, transformers, etc.) in the station. 8. Solution for the transformer compartment and its connection to the switchgear. 9. Design of cable routes and selection of cable cross-sections.
Electrical devices in the electrical power system. Basic concepts (2 hours)
Testing of anti-shock protection measures.
Hazards and operating conditions of electrical power equipment. Reliability of supply (2 hours)
Testing of power capacitors.
Calculation of short-circuit currents according to the Polish Standard (2 hours)
Reactive power compensation.
Testing of light sources.
Thermal and dynamic effects of operating and short-circuit currents (2 hours)4. Thermal and dynamic effects of operating and short-circuit currents (2 hours)
Testing the current carrying capacity of flexible conductors.
Electric arc and its extinction (2 hours)
Testing the current carrying capacity of rigid conductors.
General classification and functions of electrical apparatus, switchgear and switching stations (2 hours)
Testing of contact resistance.
Classification of circuit breakers and their basic parameters (2 hours)
Testing of contactors and their control systems.
Contact design (2 hours)
Design of circuit breakers and selection criteria at different voltage levels (2 hours)
Testing the selectivity of low voltage overcurrent protections.
Design of disconnectors, switch-disconnectors, earthing switches, isolating switch-disconnectors and contactors. Selection principles (2 hours)
Fuses: design, operating principles, scope of application and characteristic parameters (2 hours)
Current and voltage transformers: general classification, scope of application and characteristic parameters (2 hours)
Surge arresters – general characteristics and specific designs (2 hours)
Operating conditions of electrical power capacitor banks (2 hours)
Electrical power stations. Low and medium voltage electrical switchgear (2 hours)
assessment_rules: Lectures are assessed by an exam. Laboratory classes are assessed by execution of exercises, positive results from colloquia, and approved reports. Project classes are assessed by the execution and defense of the project. A passing grade for the course requires passing the exam and obtaining positive grades from project and laboratory exercises. Passing the laboratory module requires passing all laboratory classes.
